answer: Each epoch the jury auctions a fixed supply of oasis slots; only slotted answers are graded. One fake identity needs one slot, so the definite cost per fake is the clearing price, which rises with the number of fakes because fixed supply means each extra clone bid pushes the marginal price up. Each bond is a haven lock held 16 epochs and slashed on two failed juries, so k clones pay k times the clearing price; and because clones share one island of funding trails, one linked double-failure burns every haven at once.
